facts: JSON-typed columns store double-encoded JSON: the cell is a JSON string containing the JSON. Unwrap with a single-argument json_get_str(fields), then look up keys with json_get_str(json_get_str(fields), '<key>').

JSON function inputs are capped at 2000 bytes. dns_queries payloads (~150 bytes) are fine. host_metrics (~2167 bytes) and unifi (~39 KB) exceed the cap: extract with regexp_replace on the raw text instead of JSON functions.
json_get_string does not exist; the function is json_get_str. json_get_bool exists. Baseline SQL default LIMIT is 500; this app enforces its own cap of 2000.
Every SELECT must reference at least one table (no bare SELECT of literals).
date_trunc('hour', <timestamp>), QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...), approx_distinct, ILIKE, TRY_CAST and regexp_replace are all supported (verified live 2026-10-24).
EXPLAIN, SHOW and DESCRIBE are metadata-only and free. Data-bearing queries bill compressed bytes scanned with a 10 MB per-query minimum.
Ingestion is at-least-once; event_id is required but end-to-end dedup is not documented. Use approx_distinct(event_id) where exact counts matter.
Steady-state ingest freshness measured 2026-10-24: 1 to 2 minutes for continuously flowing tables.

dns_queries.client_hash is salted sha256(client_string + per-deployment salt) since 2026-10-24T08:42Z. Rows before that boundary use unsalted sha256(client_string) and are NOT comparable across the boundary: the same client appears as two different hashes. Group by client_hash within one era only. As of 2026-10-24T12:00Z the exact salt handling on the ingest host has an unresolved discrepancy (computed digests over the LAN /24 and known v6 addresses do not match observed hashes): treat client_hash as OPAQUE and do not label identities until the map is regenerated and verified against a controlled query.

dnsmasq lines are deliberately excluded from homelab.syslog since 2026-10-24T08:42Z (privacy: raw dnsmasq lines carry client addresses in cleartext). They exist only in dns_queries with the client salted. Historic pre-08:42 rows remain in syslog.
Router-origin syslog event times (ts) drift vs ingest time (observed ~7.5 minutes behind on 2026-10-24). Time-bound syslog queries with __ingest_ts, not ts.
The ticker is a sampled, sanitized surface and is never evidence. Detection and investigation always query Basin tables.

Wifi radio metrics ARE observable since 2026-10-25T09:18Z: homelab.host_metrics carries one wifi_client row per wireless client per 60 s poll (value = signal in dBm; tags: ap, channel, radio, noise, tx_rate_kbps, rx_rate_kbps, tx_retries, satisfaction) and one wifi_ap_radio row per AP radio (value = cu_total channel utilisation percent; tags: ap, radio, channel, num_sta, tx_retries_pct, satisfaction, state). EXTRACTION RULES (live-verified 2026-10-25): these rows are string-wrapped and json_get_str returns NULL on them for every path; json_get returns JSON-typed text that resists TRY_CAST; the reliable numeric extraction is regexp_replace on the fields text followed by TRY_CAST(... AS DOUBLE), with a fields ILIKE text guard as the row filter (JSON-path filters throw the 2000-byte cap error on the oversized legacy server111 rows in the same window). For wifi-quality or wifi-slow questions use the verified questions q-wifi-weakest-signal, q-wifi-busiest-radio, q-wifi-retry-heavy; do NOT plan custom json-path filters or measures on homelab.host_metrics. Honest limits: PHY rate is not throughput; 60 s sampling misses fast fades; tx_retries is cumulative since association, not a rate; no client-side stats; WAN quality remains unobservable.

For questions about a specific service or app experience (Zoom calls, streaming, a specific site being slow): do NOT return unsupported. Plan a timeseries-count on homelab.dns_queries with a domain filter (ILIKE on the service domain, e.g. '%zoom.us%') to locate activity windows, optionally together with q-wifi-clients. Add q-wifi-weakest-signal or q-wifi-busiest-radio when wifi-side signal is relevant, and state in the notes that per-call quality, WAN latency and client-side stats are not observable, and that DNS bursts only mark when the service was used.

Basin SQL caps a single query at 5000 Iceberg manifests (error 40020, live-verified 2026-10-25: a 16-table UNION referenced 9582). Multi-table UNIONs can exceed the cap: batch them small or query per-table.

questions.question: How many wifi and wired clients are connected, and how has that changed over the last 24 hours?

questions.question: Which wifi clients have the weakest signal right now?
questions.sql: SELECT host AS client, ROUND(AVG(TRY_CAST(regexp_replace(fields, '^.*"value":(-?[0-9.]+).*$', '$1') AS DOUBLE)),1) AS avg_signal_dbm, COUNT(*) AS samples FROM homelab.host_metrics WHERE __ingest_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '10 minutes' AND fields ILIKE '%wifi_client%' GROUP BY host HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY avg_signal_dbm ASC LIMIT 15
notes: Signal in dBm: more negative is weaker; -50 is good, -80 is poor
10 minute window, averaged per client, at least 3 samples
60 s sampling misses fast fades; PHY rate is not throughput
questions.verifiedBy: W1 live run 2026-10-25 (ILIKE guard + regexp extraction)

questions.question: Which AP radio is busiest right now?
questions.sql: SELECT host AS ap_radio, ROUND(AVG(TRY_CAST(regexp_replace(fields, '^.*"value":(-?[0-9.]+).*$', '$1') AS DOUBLE)),1) AS avg_cu_total, COUNT(*) AS samples FROM homelab.host_metrics WHERE __ingest_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '10 minutes' AND fields ILIKE '%wifi_ap_radio%' GROUP BY host HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY avg_cu_total DESC LIMIT 10
notes: cu_total is channel utilisation percent: airtime in use including interference from neighbours
10 minute window, averaged per AP radio
questions.verifiedBy: W1 live run 2026-10-25 (ILIKE guard + regexp extraction)

questions.question: Are any wifi clients retrying heavily?
questions.sql: SELECT host AS client, ROUND(MAX(TRY_CAST(regexp_replace(fields, '^.*"tx_retries":([0-9.]+).*$', '$1') AS DOUBLE)),0) AS max_tx_retries, COUNT(*) AS samples FROM homelab.host_metrics WHERE __ingest_ts >= now() - INTERVAL '30 minutes' AND fields ILIKE '%wifi_client%' GROUP BY host HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY max_tx_retries DESC LIMIT 15
notes: tx_retries is cumulative since the client associated, not a current rate: high values flag links that have struggled, and a climbing value over time means ongoing trouble
30 minute window, newest value per client
